claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu coating exhibits Cu segregation at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary Cu segregation weakens grain-boundary cohesion in the baseline coating.
A modified heat treatment can reduce grain-boundary Cu segregation relative to the as-deposited coating.
A minor compositional adjustment can reduce grain-boundary Cu segregation relative to the baseline coating.
Reduced formation of Cu-rich grain-boundary clusters enhances grain-boundary cohesion.
Higher grain-boundary cohesion suppresses microcrack initiation during sliding.
Higher grain-boundary cohesion suppresses localized shear banding during sliding.
Suppressing localized cracking and shear banding produces a more uniform strain distribution and more homogeneous plastic deformation.
The more homogeneous deformation mode reduces overall wear loss.
The modified coating will have a lower wear rate than the baseline coating during high-temperature sliding.
The modified coating will shift from localized shear bands with microcracking toward distributed homogeneous plastic deformation.
Grain-boundary diffusion and associated microstructural processes are significant or dominant during sliding at approximately 400–600°C.
The predicted trends may not apply outside approximately 400–600°C or under substantially different sliding conditions.
High-temperature oxidation could influence the observed deformation or wear response.
Secondary phase transformations could influence the high-temperature outcomes.
Failure to achieve reduced Cu segregation would falsify the proposed causal hypothesis.
